title: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

relationships.phenotype: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene (600047) on chromosome 9q34.

checks.claim: Intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Paper links homozygous ABCA2 truncating variants to GDD/ID but does not use the IDPOGSA disease name (poor growth, seizures, ataxia not described).

checks.claim: The ABCA2 gene is located on chromosome 9q34.
checks.evidence_quote: homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38])
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature not stated in the paper; acceptable as restatement of gene identity.

paragraphs.text: IDPOGSA is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Maddirevula et al., 2019). Some affected individuals have cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria (Aslam and Naz, 2019).

checks.claim: IDPOGSA is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Homozygous segregating variants imply recessive inheritance, but the paper does not explicitly state the inheritance mode for this disorder.

checks.claim: IDPOGSA is characterized by global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2

checks.claim: Some individuals affected by IDPOGSA have cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) described 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability. The index patient (16DG0071) did not have obvious gross dysmorphism. The authors suggested that this phenotype is a distinct allelic disorder, different from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis previously reported with ABCA2.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) described 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2

checks.claim: The index patient (16DG0071) described by Maddirevula et al. (2019) did not have obvious gross dysmorphism.
checks.evidence_quote: Facial pictures of index (16DG0071) subject with ABCA2 showing apparent lack of gross dysmorphism.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) suggested that the ABCA2-related global developmental delay and intellectual disability phenotype is a distinct allelic disorder, different from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis previously reported with ABCA2.
checks.evidence_quote: which is distinct from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reported by Steinberg et al.
checks.explanation: Class 3 = potentially distinct allelic disorders; ABCA2 included.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) reported 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family who had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria. Brain MRI of the older sib was normal. Both affected individuals had elevated levels of low density lipoproteins in the blood.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) reported 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family who had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: The methods also describe the family as a consanguineous Pakistani family with two affected siblings.

checks.claim: Brain MRI of the older of the 2 Pakistani sibs reported by Aslam and Naz (2019) was normal.
checks.evidence_quote: Magnetic resonance imaging did not reveal brain abnormalities.
checks.explanation: The methods state that MRI was done on the older sibling.

checks.claim: Both affected Pakistani sibs reported by Aslam and Naz (2019) had elevated levels of low density lipoproteins in the blood.
checks.evidence_quote: The levels of low density lipid proteins were elevated in blood samples of both affected individuals.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of IDPOGSA in the families reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019) and by Aslam and Naz (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified homozygous ABCA2 variants that fully segregated with the phenotype in 2 families, and Aslam and Naz (2019) identified a segregating ABCA2 variant in affected sibs from a consanguineous family.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of IDPOGSA in the families reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Homozygous segregation is consistent with AR inheritance, but the paper does not explicitly describe the transmission pattern.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of IDPOGSA in the family reported by Aslam and Naz (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Although recessively inherited ABCA2 variants have been reported in two patients who had intellectual disability with global developmental delays, our study demonstrates the role of an ABCA2 variant in the pathogenesis of ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: Consanguinity and two affected siblings fit recessive inheritance, but the abstract never says outright that this family's inheritance was autosomal recessive or that the variant was homozygous.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified homozygous ABCA2 variants that fully segregated with the phenotype in 2 families.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) identified an ABCA2 variant that segregated with the phenotype in affected sibs from a consanguineous family.
checks.evidence_quote: identified a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36) in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2) which segregated with the disorder
checks.explanation: Stated directly; the family is described as consanguineous.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability, Maddirevula et al. (2019) used autozygome and exome analysis to identify homozygous truncating mutations in the ABCA2 gene. In one family, they found a 1-bp duplication (c.740dupT; NM_212533.2), resulting in a frameshift and premature termination (Gly248ArgfsTer38); in the second family, they found a nonsense mutation (c.1027C-T; NM_212533.2), resulting in a gln343-to-ter (Q343X) substitution. In each family, the variant fully segregated with the phenotype.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) used autozygome and exome analysis to identify homozygous truncating ABCA2 mutations in affected members of 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Methods: autozygome and exome analysis of patients.

checks.claim: In one family, Maddirevula et al. (2019) found a 1-bp duplication in ABCA2 (c.740dupT; NM_212533.2), resulting in a frameshift and premature termination (Gly248ArgfsTer38).
checks.evidence_quote: ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38])

checks.claim: In a second family, Maddirevula et al. (2019) found an ABCA2 nonsense mutation (c.1027C-T; NM_212533.2), resulting in a Q343X substitution.
Each of the ABCA2 variants c.740dupT and c.1027C-T fully segregated with the phenotype in its respective family reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019).
checks.evidence_quote: fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38]) and (NM_212533.2:c.1027C>T:p.[Gln343*])

paragraphs.text: In 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with ataxia and dysarthria, Aslam and Naz (2019) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a 1-bp deletion in the ABCA2 gene (c.4993delG; NM_212533.2), resulting in a frameshift and premature termination (Val1665TyrfsTer36). Sanger sequencing showed that the mutation segregated with the disorder. It was absent from all publicly available databases and from ethnically matched controls.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a 1-bp deletion in ABCA2 (c.4993delG; NM_212533.2) in 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with ataxia and dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing data analyses identified a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36) in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2)

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.4993delG deletion results in a frameshift and premature termination (Val1665TyrfsTer36).
checks.evidence_quote: a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36)
checks.explanation: The notation fsTer36 means a frameshift ending in a premature stop codon.

checks.claim: Sanger sequencing showed that the ABCA2 c.4993delG mutation segregated with the disorder in the Pakistani family.
checks.evidence_quote: Segregation of variants with the phenotype was checked by Sanger sequencing.
checks.explanation: The results state that the variant segregated with the disorder.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.4993delG mutation was absent from all publicly available databases.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) noted that recessive ABCA2 variants had previously been reported in patients with intellectual disability and global developmental delay. They concluded that their family showed a distinct ataxia-with-dysarthria phenotype, reflecting pleiotropic effects of ABCA2 mutation, and stated that the phenotype closely matched that of Abca2 knockout mice.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) noted that recessive ABCA2 variants had previously been reported in patients with intellectual disability and global developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: recessively inherited ABCA2 variants have been reported in two patients who had intellectual disability with global developmental delays

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) concluded that their Pakistani family showed a distinct ataxia-with-dysarthria phenotype reflecting pleiotropic effects of ABCA2 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Our research links an ABCA2 variant with a distinct form of ataxia with dysarthria in humans and demonstrates pleiotropic effects due to the gene mutation.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) stated that the ataxia-with-dysarthria phenotype in their family closely matched that of Abca2 knockout mice.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenotype observed in our patients shows high concordance with that observed in Abca2 knockout mice.
checks.explanation: "High concordance" means the same as "closely matched".
